claims.text: Integrating machine learning with high-throughput computational screening enables rapid identification of RHEA compositions.
The identified RHEA compositions can provide a better balance of strength, ductility, and density than compositions designed solely through thermo-kinetic simulations.
Atomic-size mismatch, mixing enthalpy, valence electron concentration, and related electronic or structural factors are suitable descriptors for screening RHEA compositions.
Machine-learning screening can be integrated with high-throughput simulations for RHEA composition design.
Atomic-size difference, mixing enthalpy, and valence electron concentration are correlated with mechanical-performance parameters.
A model trained on existing data can learn relationships between atomic-scale descriptors and mechanical properties.
Learned descriptor-property relationships can rapidly identify compositions expected to combine high intrinsic strength, ductility, and low density.
Machine-learning-selected RHEAs will exhibit statistically significant improvements in strength when compared with conventionally designed RHEAs.
Machine-learning-selected RHEAs will exhibit statistically significant improvements in ductility when compared with conventionally designed RHEAs.
Machine-learning-selected RHEAs will have lower density than conventionally designed RHEAs.
The effectiveness of the machine-learning predictions is limited to the composition and processing domains represented in the training data.
Predictions for compositions outside the training range or for extreme processing conditions are uncertain.
